body:
@vvo This is just an implementation detail. If you want to separate into two API methods you can do that; if you want to have more of a middleware concept, which I think is a more elegant solution, whether it checks that each middleware returned true/false or called a callback you provided is up to you.

Plus, the return pattern is a very simple way to achieve what we want, and easily documented too (`return false if you want to cancel the current search`), and no-one is actually going to need to "listen" to the return value but your own internal code. So to me that's not that big of an issue.
